statement.p: Compute the length of the curve {\bf r\it(t)} = 5 t {\bf \, i} + 9 t {\bf \, j} +(t^2 - 1){\bf \, k} over the interval 0 \le t \le 4.
HINT: use the formula \int \sqrt{ t^2 + a^2} \, dt = \frac{1}{2} t \sqrt{t^2+a^2} + \frac{1}{2} a^2 \ln \left( t + \sqrt{t^2+a^2} \right) + C

static.solution:
\bf r\it(t) is \bf r\it'(t)=5 {\bf \, i}+9{\bf \, j}+2t{\bf \, k}.Using the Arc Length Formula we get: L = \int_0^{4} \left||\bf r\it'(t)\right||\,dt =\int_0^{4} \sqrt{{5}^2+{9}^2+(2t)^2}\,dt =\int_0^{4}\sqrt{4t^2+106}\,dt We substitute u=2t, \,du=2\,dt and use the given integration formula. This gives: L=\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{8}\sqrt{u^2+106}\,du= \left.\frac{1}{4}u\sqrt{u^2+106}+\frac{1}{4}\cdot 106\ln\left(u+\sqrt{u^2+106}\right)\right|_0^{8}=
\frac{1}{4}8\sqrt{{8}^2+106}+\frac{106}{4}\ln\left(8+\sqrt{{8}^2+106}\right) - \frac{106}{4}\ln\sqrt{106}
=\frac{4}{2}\sqrt{170}+\frac{106}{4}\ln\left(8+\sqrt{170}\right) - \frac{106}{4}\ln\sqrt{106}=
\frac{4}{2}\sqrt{170}+\frac{106}{4}\ln\frac{8+\sqrt{170}}{\sqrt{106}} \approx 45.01
